purpose: Every ACCEPTED entity-versus-database difference, with a reason and the section that accepted it.
A difference NOT recorded here fails `npm run check:entity-contract`. A recorded entry whose
difference has gone is reported as STALE so the ledger stays honest.
This is a LEDGER, not a suppression list. Its purpose is that a difference nobody has decided
about cannot ship silently, and that SC-2's two contradiction classes cannot silently return:
there is deliberately NO entry here for a standards_master length or for a timestamp type, so
either one coming back fails the gate.

sc2ClosedAt309.contradiction1: standards_master — six columns whose entity declarations omitted the bounds migration 1800000004000 deliberately authored. REPAIRED in the entity. No ledger entry exists for them, so a regression fails the gate.
sc2ClosedAt309.contradiction2: site.createdAt, inspection.createdAt, user.deletedAt, user.nextBillingDate — entity declared timestamptz over a `timestamp without time zone` column. REPAIRED in the entity. No ledger entry exists for them either.

sc3ClosedAt310.outcome: The four TABLE_MISSING_IN_DB entries are removed because the ENTITIES are gone, not because the tables were created.
sc3ClosedAt310.classification: All four families were classified B — LEGACY / SUPERSEDED ARCHITECTURE. Each has a shipping canonical successor: `report`/`finding` -> `inspection_reports` + `inspection_report_versions` + `inspection_findings`; `report_attachments` -> inspection evidence storage; `hazard_taxonomy` -> the shipped taxonomy JSON map read by HazardTaxonomyCoverageService via fs.readFileSync, which never used a database table.
sc3ClosedAt310.whyNotCreateTheTables: §310 forbids resurrecting retired architecture merely to eliminate a 500. Creating `report` and `finding` would have re-established a mutable report model that §305A and the immutable-report work deliberately replaced, and would have produced a second, divergent source of report truth.
theHonestyProblem: Removing an entity makes this gate stop comparing it, so a shrinking entity set could make the gate green without anything being repaired.

That is why the entities removed in §310 are ENUMERATED below rather than merely deleted, and why the SC-3 closure rests on the ROUTE PROOF — `npm run test:310-missing-relation:db` drives every affected deployed route against a live replayed database and asserts no 5xx — rather than on this gate going quiet.

The canonical schema gate (`check:canonical-schema`) is unaffected by entity removal: it compares a replayed database against the committed manifest and would still fail if a table the manifest describes went missing.

entitiesRemoved.note: Was never registered in the application DataSource, so no deployed route could reach it; a second, conflicting definition of the same table name also existed in src/intelligence-library.

sc3ClosedAt310.routesRetired: Every deployed route whose handler chain read one of these tables now answers 410 Gone rather than 500. 410 rather than 404 because the surviving routes are namespaced `legacy/`, which earlier sections established as a deliberate compatibility signal, and six sibling routes already answered 410.

sc4SubscriptionStatusResolvedAt310.outcome: The COLUMN_DEFAULT entry for user.subscriptionStatus is removed because the DATABASE was repaired, not because the comparison stopped.
sc4SubscriptionStatusResolvedAt310.change: ALTER TABLE "user" ALTER COLUMN "subscriptionStatus" SET DEFAULT 'none' — the entity already declared 'none', so the entity was correct and the database was wrong.
sc4SubscriptionStatusResolvedAt310.whyItMattered: 'active' is the one value the entitlement layer reads as a paying customer. A default is the value you get when nobody decided, and it granted entitlement on silence.
sc4SubscriptionStatusResolvedAt310.deliberatelyNotDone: No existing row was read or rewritten. Existing 'active' rows are legitimate customer subscription state and a migration cannot distinguish those from rows that inherited the bad default. The objective was DEFAULT correction, not customer-state normalization.
sc4SubscriptionStatusResolvedAt310.stillOpen: SC-4 remains OPEN. The eleven other registered SC-4 differences are unchanged and still carry their §309 reasons; only this one member was in §310's scope.

entries.reason: SC-4. The database holds `character varying`; the entity declares `uuid`. Postgres accepts a uuid-shaped string into varchar, so writes succeed and reads return the string — but the two types compare and sort differently, and a varchar column cannot reject a malformed identifier the way uuid does. Not repaired in §309: changing the column is a migration on customer data and changing the entity would weaken a declared type, so it is a decision rather than a transcription.

SC-4. The database permits NULL; the entity declares NOT NULL. The application always supplies it, so no NULL row exists on the Beta v1 path — but the entity is asserting a guarantee the column does not enforce, which is the same shape as the SC-2 timestamp claim §309 just removed. Tightening the column is a migration; loosening the entity weakens a true invariant. Registered rather than guessed.

SC-4. The database is NOT NULL with DEFAULT 'reference'; the entity declares nullable. A write omitting it receives the default rather than NULL, so the entity's nullability is unreachable in practice. HazLenz knowledge, not on the Beta v1 individual path.

SC-4. The database default is 'basic'; the entity declares 'free'. `basic` is one of the legacy values the product normalizes to 'pro'. Same containment as subscriptionStatus: registration sets `planCode: 'free'` explicitly, so the default is never reached.

SC-4. The database default is 3 (lowest authority); the entity declares 1 (highest). The directions are opposite, so a row created without an explicit tier would be trusted very differently depending on which contract answered. HazLenz knowledge ingestion always sets it, and it is not on the Beta v1 individual path — but the disagreement is semantic rather than cosmetic, which is why it is registered rather than silently aligned.
SC-4. The database has DEFAULT 'reference'; the entity declares none. Pairs with the nullability entry above.

SC-4. The database has DEFAULT now(); the entity declares none. The service always supplies the decision time, so the default is a safety net rather than a behaviour. Harmless, and recorded so the gate stays quiet about it without anybody having to remember why.

SC-4. A legacy column the current entity no longer declares. A DB-extra column is not a runtime failure — nothing reads it — it means a stored value is invisible to the application. Dropping it would be a destructive migration on a log table for no functional gain.
SC-4. Legacy column superseded by `retrievedChunkIds` / `selectedChunkIds`, both of which the entity declares and the database has.
SC-4. Legacy column superseded by `queryText`, which the entity declares and the database has NOT NULL.
SC-4. Legacy column; the entity no longer declares it.
